analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: the morning's earnings prints all landed, and they split. Palo Alto is the standout — a clean beat-and-raise (+39% revenue, FY27 guide lifted) good for ~+10% premarket and a sector-wide cyber rally. PDD also beat on profit (adj. EPS ¥21.04 vs ~¥18.5-19.0) despite a revenue miss, up ~5% premarket. Alibaba is the mirror image: AI cloud revenue +53% and a revenue beat, but adjusted EPS missed and AI-lab losses tripled, shares ~-2%. Walmart flipped from the early read — after an initial 'edged higher' it is now down ~1% as the market focuses on a narrow earnings miss despite the revenue beat and raised guide. The 8:30 AM ET data added a soft note: initial claims 203K (a touch above the ~198K forecast, still near historic lows) and the Philly Fed at 6.3 vs ~20.6 expected — a sharp manufacturing miss, though from a single calendar screenshot so far, so treat the Philly print as provisional until a second outlet confirms it. Futures held the pop (Nasdaq-100 +2.2%, S&P +1.3%, Dow +0.7%) and the 10-year ticked up to 5.11%. The Anthropic debut remains the day's center of gravity, with ANT trading starting today. Signal vs noise: the PANW print, the claims/Philly data, and the futures tape are signal; the exact size of premarket moves (PDD +5% vs +10% in early prints) and the ANT opening print are noise until the cash session confirms them.

community_signals.takeaway: The 922-comment Anthropic IPO thread remains the live debate, now reframed by the confirmed $83 price and the $26B supplier private placement: 'priced for perfection' skepticism at ~$1.5T vs AI-scarcity enthusiasm. It frames how the market may read ANT's first trade today.

community_signals.takeaway: A research firm's 'unprecedented test of investor gullibility' framing of the IPO (217 comments) is the counterweight in the same debate — the valuation-versus-fundamentals argument that will be tested by today's first trade.

headlines.headline: Futures hold the rebound into the open: Nasdaq-100 +2.2%, S&P 500 +1.3%, Dow +0.7% (Investopedia, ~8:30 AM ET). The 10-year Treasury is 5.11%, up from 5.08% at Wednesday's close. WTI ~$84.10 (+1%). Prior session: S&P -0.23% for a fifth straight down day, Dow -1.11% for a third straight >1% drop, Nasdaq +0.42%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The snapback is holding into the open rather than fading — breadth at 9:30 AM ET will show whether this is a durable turn or a premarket relief pop.

headlines.headline: 8:30 AM ET data: initial jobless claims 203K for the week ending Nov 14, slightly above the ~198K forecast and up from 200K (revised to 202K) the prior week. The Philly Fed manufacturing index printed 6.3 vs ~20.6 expected and 20.9 prior — a sharp downside miss.
headlines.why_it_matters: Claims are DOL-confirmed and still near historic lows, which keeps the hawkish frame intact; the Philly Fed miss is single-source (economic-calendar screenshot) and unconfirmed by a second outlet so far — treat it as provisional, but if it holds it is a soft manufacturing read against the rate-hike case.

headlines.headline: Palo Alto Networks (PANW) +9-10% premarket after a beat-and-raise: fiscal Q1 revenue $3.445B (+39% YoY) vs ~$3.31B expected, adjusted EPS $1.05 vs $0.97, Next-Generation Security ARR +66%. FY27 revenue guide lifted to $14.52-14.57B (from ~$14.2B expected) and non-GAAP EPS to $4.26-4.30. Also announced a $4.5B acquisition of Applied Compute. CrowdStrike +6% premarket in sympathy.
headlines.why_it_matters: A clean beat-and-raise with a raised full-year guide is the strongest kind of earnings catalyst — and it is lifting the whole cybersecurity sector, not just PANW.

headlines.headline: Alibaba (BABA) ~-2% premarket after a split print: revenue RMB271.52B (+10% YoY) beat the ~RMB269.8B estimate and AI cloud revenue jumped 53% to RMB60.97B, but adjusted EPS of RMB8.10 ($1.21) missed the ~RMB11.16 ($1.65) expected. Cloud EBITA more than doubled to RMB8.83B, while AI-lab losses tripled to a RMB10.5B loss on heavy R&D and inference costs. Free cash flow was a RMB34.47B outflow.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI cloud growth story is real (+53%), but the market is pricing the cost of it — tripling AI-lab losses and a cash outflow — so the EPS miss is doing the work this morning.

headlines.headline: PDD Holdings (PDD) +4.6% premarket (Finnhub, 8:58 AM ET; early prints had it up ~10%) after Q3 profit beat: adjusted EPS RMB21.04 per ADS vs ~RMB18.5-19.0 expected, adjusted operating profit RMB32.6B vs ~RMB27.9B expected. Revenue was flat at RMB108.3B and missed the ~RMB115-116B consensus; transaction services revenue fell 12% while online marketing rose 12%. Operating expenses fell 12% on a 17% cut in sales and marketing spend.
headlines.why_it_matters: A profit beat driven by cost cuts rather than growth — the market is rewarding the margin discipline for now, but flat revenue caps how far the re-rating can run.

headlines.headline: Walmart (WMT) down ~1% premarket after its Q3 results — a cooler reception than the early-morning read. Revenue beat expectations and full-year guidance was raised, but earnings narrowly missed estimates per Investopedia, and shares have been under pressure since last quarter's softer outlook.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest U.S. retailer beat on sales and raised guidance yet still slipped — the market is grading the earnings line, not the top line, into the holidays.

headlines.headline: Microsoft (MSFT) +0.9-1% premarket after a bullish Stifel upgrade — the firm writes Microsoft is 'getting back on track.'
headlines.why_it_matters: An analyst upgrade is a modest tailwind on a stock already riding the AI rebound — single-source via a ZeroHedge premarket-movers post, so the upgrade framing is unconfirmed by a second outlet.

headlines.headline: Mag 7 premarket movers: Nvidia +1.6%, Tesla +1.1%, Microsoft +1%, Amazon +0.6%, Alphabet +0.6%, Meta +0.3%, while Apple falls ~2% after reports it cut component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max on weaker-than-expected demand.
headlines.why_it_matters: Six of seven Mag 7 names are green into the open — the rebound is broad, not just an index future. Apple remains the lone divergence, and its demand story is still single-source and unconfirmed by Apple.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) begins trading on the Nasdaq today after pricing its IPO at $83 a share — above the $70-78 range — in an $81B offering, the largest on record, for a ~$1.5T valuation. Alongside it, a $26B private placement at $83 was bought by seven suppliers (Google $10B, Nvidia $10B, AMD $2.5B, Broadcom $1B, Micron $1B, Microsoft $1B, TSMC $0.5B). Demand ran to nearly 7x the shares on offer; 315M insider shares are eligible to sell from day one.
headlines.why_it_matters: The day's center of gravity — the first trade prices the debate over whether the AI supply chain buying its biggest customer's equity is partnership or circularity, and day-one insider supply is a real overhang.
